why_go: Peak Goa winter: 21–31°C, dry. Post-NYE gridlock eases Jan 5. Tito's Lane runs nightly, Strip at full chaos with water sports. Go for the party scene.
Goa's driest month: 22–32°C. Traffic and nightlife at full operations, rates stable. Carnival energy reaches Mapusa 8km inland. Beach watersports peak.
Last cool window before heat: 23–33°C. Hotel rates slide 20–25%. Holi week mid-month brings traffic spike but water sports remain ideal throughout.
Pre-monsoon heat 25–35°C, 75% humidity peaks April. Beach viable before 10am and after 5pm. Strip evening atmosphere intact but midday collapse.
why_not: April heat spikes to 35°C+; extended beach time requires early/late windows; midday exposure risky.

why_go: Peak pre-monsoon: 26–36°C, 80% humidity. Evening strip still functions. Shacks dismantle May 31. Thunder storm weeks 3–4 loom.
why_not: Pre-monsoon humidity peaks making beach time compressed to dawn and dusk; afternoon unbearably hot.
SW monsoon arrives June 10: 24–30°C, 700–800mm rain. Shacks closed entirely, sea unsafe for swimming, water sports suspended completely.
Peak monsoon: 24–29°C, 900–1100mm rainfall. Beach officially closed, commercial strip dormant, sea completely impassable and dangerous.
Monsoon continues: 24–29°C, 500–700mm rain. Strip remains dormant, sea hazardous throughout month, tourism infrastructure shuttered.

why_go: Monsoon retreat: 24–31°C, 250–300mm rain. Shacks rebuilding for Oct 1 reopen. Some restaurants resume service late-month.
why_not: Monsoon debris clutters sand; shacks mid-reconstruction; beach still rough; swimming unsafe mid-month.

why_go: Season reopens Oct 1: 24–32°C, 100–150mm late spillover. Shacks rebuilt, water sports resume week two. Comfortable temperatures return.
Peak builds: 22–31°C, <30mm rain. Saturday Night Market resumes. Tito's Lane at full rhythm. Rates 20–30% below December peak.
Peak Goa: 21–30°C, dry. Christmas-NYE rates 2–3x. Strip gridlocks Dec 22–Jan 5. Sunburn diaspora at Vagator pulls 80,000+ weekend days.
Peak Goa winter: 21–30°C, dry. Calmer beach than Calangute; resort spine of North Goa. Bomra's (CNT Top 50 2024) booking 5–7 days out.
Driest month: 22–31°C. Fort Aguada (1612) at south end; Aguada lighthouse (1864) open. Carnival reaches Mapusa; family-friendly crowd dominates.
Last cool window: 23–32°C. Hotel rates slide 20%. Holi week mid-month traffic spike. Lifeguarded, calm sea for swimmers throughout.
Pre-monsoon heat 25–34°C, 75% humidity. Fort Aguada walk collapses mid-day but early/late windows workable.
why_not: April heat spikes; Fort Aguada walk unviable 10am–5pm; humidity exhausting for extended sightseeing.

why_go: Peak heat 26–35°C, 80% humidity. Shacks dismantle May 31. Pre-monsoon thunder weeks 3–4. Early swimming possible.
why_not: Peak pre-monsoon: extreme heat, 80%+ humidity, shacks dismantling, water unsafe, exhausting conditions.
SW monsoon arrives: 24–30°C, 700–800mm rain. Shacks closed, sea closed, watersports suspended entirely.
Peak monsoon: 24–29°C, 900–1100mm rain. Beach closed, strip dormant, sea completely impassable.

why_go: Monsoon eases late-month: 24–29°C, 500–700mm rain. Bomra's reopens around Aug 15; restaurant village rebuilds.
why_not: Monsoon remains active; swimming unsafe; beach debris; limited water sports.

why_go: Monsoon retreat: 24–31°C, 250–300mm rain. Restaurant village fully open by mid-Sep. Beach rebuilding.
why_not: Monsoon debris, rough seas, humidity linger; beach reconstruction ongoing; swimming unsafe.

why_go: Season reopens Oct 1: 24–31°C, 100–150mm late spillover. Shacks rebuilt, water sports return week two. Calm seas.
Peak builds: 22–30°C, <30mm rain. Bomra's booking lead 5–7 days. Stone House at peak nightly demand.
Peak Goa: 21–30°C, dry. Christmas-NYE rates 2–3x. Bomra's booking 10–14 days. Less Sunburn-spillover than Vagator.

why_not: Frozen and inaccessible: –25 to –10°C. Kunzum Pass under 6+ feet of snow. No road access, no camps, no visit possible.
Year's coldest: –28 to –12°C. Lake frozen, no road access, no camps. Roads completely snowbound throughout.
Still snowbound: –22 to –5°C. BRO clearance starting but lake frozen. Road impossible until May clearance.
BRO clearance underway: –15 to 2°C. Roads 6–8 weeks from opening. Lake melt starting but access blocked.
Road unpredictable until late May: –8 to 8°C. Kaza side may open late 4×4-only. Camps not yet operational.

why_go: Season opens: 0–15°C. Camps deploying mid-month. Manali approach opens late-May/early-June. Reliable road access.
why_not: Lake thaws gradually; expect partial ice and limited camping accessibility early-month.

why_go: Peak summer: 3–17°C. Both road approaches reliable. Camps at full capacity. Turquoise-to-blue colour shifts visible.
Peak summer continues: 3–17°C. Kaza side reliable, camps deployed fully. Manali side landslide risk managed.
Best month: 0–15°C, dry, monsoon retreating. Camps still deployed. Cleanest air quality of the year.
Season closes: –8 to 10°C. Camps wind down first week. First snowfall arrives mid-month on Kunzum.
why_not: Snow arrival cuts trekking window to early October before conditions deteriorate sharply.
Closed for winter: –15 to 2°C. Both approaches snow-blocked. No road, no camps. Access forbidden entirely.
Frozen and inaccessible: –22 to –5°C. Lake re-frozen. No road, no camps. All access routes closed.

why_go: Peak winter: 10–24°C. Clear skies, pleasant walking weather. UNESCO moidams explored comfortably year-best.
Late winter: 12–26°C. Dry, comfortable walking. Royal mound exploration at year-best comfort levels.
Spring: 15–30°C. Warming up, still dry. Ahom Dynasty heritage walk at comfortable pace and temperature.
Pre-monsoon: 18–33°C. Occasional rain mid-month. Morning exploration viable before afternoon thunder.
why_not: Pre-monsoon thunderstorms risk disrupting outdoor moidam exploration mid-morning.
Hot and humid: 22–34°C. Pre-monsoon storms. Muddy paths disruptive for archaeological site walking.
Monsoon arrives: 24–33°C, heavy rain. Muddy paths and leeches make archaeological mounds difficult.
Peak monsoon: 25–33°C, continuous rain. Waterlogged terrain makes moidam access treacherous.
Late monsoon: 25–33°C, very wet. Waterlogged pathways make moidam complex exploration difficult.

why_go: Post-monsoon: 24–32°C. Rain tapering off. Humidity lingers but paths beginning to dry.
why_not: Humidity persists; pathways still waterlogged; leeches active; exploration uncomfortable.

why_go: Autumn: 20–30°C. Dry settling in. Moidam heritage walk at comfortable temperatures and conditions.
Early winter: 14–28°C. Clear, dry, perfect. Royal burial mounds fully explored in ideal conditions.
Winter: 10–24°C. Cool, clear, dry. UNESCO heritage site at peak comfort and visibility.
Margazhi music tail + Pongal: 21–29°C, dry. Marina at full evening rotation. Music Academy till Jan 15.
Driest month: 21–30°C. Heritage walking peak season. Thai Pusam Feb 1, 2026 at Marudhamalai. Comfortable pace.
Last cool month: 24–33°C, humidity climbing steadily. Heritage walks viable till 11am and after 5pm still.
Heat dome opens: 27–37°C, 75% humidity. Tamil New Year Apr 14. Early morning walks possible.
why_not: April heat peaks 40°C with 95% humidity; outdoor exploration exhausting midday completely.

why_go: Peak heat: 29–39°C, 75% humidity. Hotel rates at year-low. Pre-dawn temple visits viable.
why_not: Peak heat and humidity make outdoor exploration exhausting; extended midday exposure risky.

why_go: SW monsoon weak on TN coast: 27–37°C, 50–80mm rain. Sea breeze slight improvement. Heat continues.
why_not: Monsoon rains and oppressive heat make June unbearably humid for extended sightseeing.

why_go: SW monsoon tail: 26–35°C, 100–130mm rain. Aadi Perukku Aug 3 anchor. Heat eases slightly.
why_not: Monsoon rains and oppressive heat make outdoor exploration difficult and uncomfortable.

why_go: Aadi continues: 26–34°C, 130–160mm rain. Aadi Perukku Cauvery anchor. Madras Day Aug 22.
why_not: Monsoon rains and 90%+ humidity make August oppressively wet and uncomfortable.

why_go: Pre-NE-monsoon: 25–33°C, 130–180mm rain. Vinayaka Chathurthi Sep 7, 2026. Heat easing.
why_not: Monsoon rains and 90%+ humidity make this the hottest, wettest month of the year.

why_go: NE monsoon arrives: 24–32°C, 250–350mm rain. Cyclone watch begins. Some heritage walks viable.
why_not: Northeast monsoon rains flood streets and disrupt walking routes mid-month completely.

why_go: NE monsoon eases: 23–30°C, 350–400mm rain. Karthigai Deepam late-month. Hotel rates climbing.
Margazhi music season + NE tail: 22–29°C, 200–250mm rain. Music Academy at peak. Cyclone.
Peak Kerala coast: 23–31°C, dry, sea calm. Spinner dolphin sightings near-daily off Cherai shore.
Driest month: 24–32°C. Dolphin sightings peak. Long-stay rate negotiations open mid-month.
Last cool month: 25–33°C. Dolphin sightings still strong. Hotel rates slide 20% from peak.
Pre-monsoon heat: 27–34°C, 80% humidity. Sea bathing viable before 9am. Vishu Apr 14.
why_not: Humidity and heat make extended beach time uncomfortable despite warm water and dolphins.

why_go: Peak heat + pre-monsoon: 28–34°C, 85% humidity. Sea state weakens. Swimming windows narrow.
why_not: Pre-monsoon swells and frequent swim restrictions limit safe bathing windows significantly.
SW monsoon arrives June 1: 25–30°C, 700–800mm rainfall. Beach unsafe, dolphin tours suspended.
Peak monsoon: 25–29°C, 800–900mm rainfall. Beach closed, dolphin tours off. Karkidakam inland.
Monsoon + Onam: 25–29°C, 500–600mm rain. Beach closed, visibility poor. Onam Aug 25.

why_go: Monsoon retreat: 25–30°C, 350–400mm rain. Sea state still rough. Onam tail; dolphins pause.
why_not: Monsoon rains and rough seas make swimming unsafe; dolphin tours still suspended.

why_go: Beach reopens Oct 1: 24–31°C, 200–250mm late spillover. Dolphin tours resume. Swimming returns.
why_not: Post-monsoon seas rough with swim warnings; dolphins return gradually mid-month.

why_go: Peak builds: 23–30°C, <50mm rain. Dolphin sightings near-daily. Rates 20% below Dec peak.
Peak season: 22–30°C, dry. Christmas-NYE rates 2–3x. Dolphin sightings at year-best.
Dry season: 5–15°C. Clear views of Bangladesh plains. Root bridge treks safest now.
why_not: Waterfalls run low despite safest conditions for root bridge trekking and clearest views.

why_go: Dry: 6–17°C. Warming up. Excellent trekking conditions. Clear canyon views. Nohkalikai flows.
Warming: 8–20°C. Pre-monsoon. Good trekking. Light showers possible late March. Waterfall buildup.
Warming: 10–22°C. Pre-monsoon showers increasing. Waterfalls building. Tourist season peaks.
why_not: Pre-monsoon rains make trails dangerously slippery while waterfalls peak flow rate.
Monsoon building: 12–22°C, heavy showers. Treks becoming risky. Waterfalls spectacular.
Full monsoon: 14–20°C, 2000mm+ this month. Roads frequently close, stranding visitors days.
Peak monsoon wettest month: 14–20°C, record rainfall. Hiking and sightseeing nearly impossible.
Heavy monsoon continues: 14–20°C, extreme rainfall. Roads too unstable for safe travel.
Retreating monsoon: 12–22°C, decreasing rain. Trails too waterlogged despite peak green.

why_go: Post-monsoon: 10–22°C. Dry, clear, waterfalls still flowing. Perfect trekking conditions.
Dry: 8–20°C. Clear views. Waterfalls still flowing. Root bridge treks optimal conditions.
Dry: 5–18°C. Clear but cold. Waterfalls reducing. Good trekking. Root bridges stable.
Peak + Pongal cluster: 20–30°C. Karaikudi mansion walks comfortable. Athangudi tile workshops open.
Driest month: 21–32°C. Mansion walks at year-best comfort. Rates ease 15% off Pongal peak.
Last cool month: 23–35°C. Mansion walks compress mid-day. Rates ease 25% below peak.
Heat dome: 26–38°C. Mansion exteriors mid-day unworkable. Early/late windows viable.
why_not: Peak heat and humidity make April nearly unbearable at sea level for exploration.

why_go: Heat peak: 27–40°C. Hotels at year-low rates. Pre-dawn mansion tours possible.
why_not: Brutal peak heat makes May unbearable at sea level; mid-day exploration impossible.

why_go: SW spillover eases: 26–37°C. Mansion walks workable mornings. Hotels recovering. Heat more bearable.
why_not: Oppressive heat and humidity make exploration physically exhausting in June.

why_go: Heat eases further: 25–35°C. Aadi-month family rituals at mansion shrines. Walks workable.
why_not: Monsoon rains make July oppressively humid; heritage site tours difficult.

why_go: Aadi tail + early NE hints: 24–33°C. Mansion walks comfortable. Diaspora returns. Temples busy.
why_not: Monsoon rains make August roads impassable; heritage sites inaccessible.

why_go: Pre-NE-monsoon: 24–32°C. Navarathri family observances. Heritage stays in demand.
why_not: Monsoon rains and humidity make September poorly suited for architecture tours.

why_go: NE arrives mid-Oct: 22–30°C. Mansion walks at year-best comfort. Aadi diaspora returns.
why_not: Early monsoon means dust storms mid-walk and sudden downpours—plan indoor tours.

why_go: Peak builds: 21–29°C, 200–250mm NE monsoon. Diwali + Karthigai Deepam. Hotels in demand.
Peak season: 20–28°C, NE wraps mid-Dec. Christmas-NYE diaspora at year-densest.
Peak Nataraja temple window: 22–29°C, dry. Pradosham nights, dawn abhishekam. Margazhi tail.
Driest month + Natyanjali in Maha Shivaratri week: 22–30°C. Five days classical dance at temple.
Natyanjali tail + heat building: 25–32°C. Maha Shivaratri week likely February 2026 — verify.
Pre-monsoon heat: 27–36°C, 78% humidity. Tamil New Year Apr 14. Temple windows compress.
why_not: Brutal heat and humidity make temple visits uncomfortable in April.

why_go: Peak heat: 29–39°C. Thunder storms last 10 days pre-monsoon. Temple pre-dawn only viable.
why_not: Extreme heat and humidity make temple visits physically taxing in May.

why_go: SW monsoon weak: 27–35°C, 50–70mm rain. Heat continues. Temple pre-dawn only.
why_not: Monsoon rains and extreme heat make June nearly unbearable for temple visits.

why_go: SW residual: 26–33°C, 100–130mm rain. Aadi opens. Heat retreating slowly.
why_not: Monsoon rains drench Tamil Nadu in July; temple visits uncomfortable.

why_go: Aadi Perukku Aug 3: 26–32°C, 130–160mm rain. Cauvery delta at peak Aadi traffic.
why_not: Monsoon rains flood temple town during August; visits uncomfortable.

why_go: Pre-NE-monsoon: 25–31°C, 130–180mm rain. Vinayaka Chathurthi Sep 7. Heat easing.
why_not: Monsoon rains make temple visits uncomfortable; pathways waterlogged.

why_go: Season opens: 24–30°C, 250–330mm rain. NE monsoon arrives. Cyclone watch begins.
why_not: Northeast monsoon rains flood town streets; temples accessible but damp.

why_go: High season: 22–29°C, 300–380mm rain. Karthigai Deepam late-month. Cyclone watch.
Peak season + Karthigai Deepam Dec 4 + Margazhi tail: 21–28°C, 150–220mm rain.
